Q: How to merge specific rows in a pandas DataFrame? A:

Found the error.

Accessing a specific cell in my dataset returns a 1x1 DataFrame. When I try to naively sum these values, python fails and returns NaN. The fix is to add .values at the end of the cells. So:



for k in range(2000,2004):
    df.loc[df['name']=="A new",str(k)]=df.loc[df['name']=="A new"][str(k)].replace('',0).astype(int).values+df.loc[df['name']=="A old"][str(k)].replace('',0).astype(int).values

Q: How to append multiple rows' data to related parent table rows without iterated queries with CodeIgniter's query builder A:

From what I get of your question you're looking to join the tables. I think you should be able to do something like this: 

SELECT test_table.test_name,
       qestion_table.question, 
       answer_table.answers 
FROM test_table
INNER JOIN questions_table 
on questions_table.id_test = test_table.id_test
INNER JOIN answers_table
ON answers_table.id_quest = questions_table.id_quest
WHERE test_table.id_test = ?

This should return the entire result set as one object rather than having to query the db several times.

Q: Can a bash script tell if it's being run via cron? A:

I needed to know if a script was run from a terminal, not by another script nor by cron.

After many tests, I ended up with this condition :

! ([ "$TERM" = "dumb" ] || [ -z "$TERM" ] || [ "$SHLVL" -gt "2" ])

which is true if and only if the script is run from a terminal.

  • "dumb" is the normal TERM value set by cron; in most cases, this condition should be sufficient to know if the script was run by cron.

  • -z $TERM is kept as a security, in case TERM would be undefined or empty which is less supposed to happen if the script is run from a terminal or by anything run by a terminal.

$SHLVL is "1" if the script is run by cron, "2" if ran by a script ran by cron and so on.

So, testing this variable value is useless to check if the script was run by cron. I keep it because I also need to know if the script is run from a terminal.

Q: Django Channels redis.exceptions.TimeoutError: Timeout reading from 127.0.0.1:6379 A:

The fact that your channel_layer.send/receive works in manage.py shell but the WebSocket times out is the tell: Redis itself is fine — your ASGI application isn't being invoked. Django is almost certainly serving the request via WSGI (which can't do WebSockets) instead of ASGI.

The four things to check, in order:

  1. ASGI_APPLICATION not set in settings (most common). Without it, Django never routes to Channels:

    python

    ASGI_APPLICATION = "myproject.asgi.application"

  2. asgi.py missing or missing a ProtocolTypeRouter:

    python

    # myproject/asgi.py

    import os

    from django.core.asgi import get_asgi_application

    from channels.routing import ProtocolTypeRouter, URLRouter

    from channels.auth import AuthMiddlewareStack

    import myproject.routing

    os.environ.setdefault("DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE", "myproject.settings")

    application = ProtocolTypeRouter({

    "http": get_asgi_application(),

    "websocket": AuthMiddlewareStack(

    URLRouter(myproject.routing.websocket_urlpatterns)

    ),

    })

  3. Running runserver without daphne in INSTALLED_APPS — the old WSGI runserver silently ignores WebSockets. Either pip install daphne and add it to INSTALLED_APPS before django.contrib.staticfiles, or run via daphne -b 0.0.0.0 -p 8000 myproject.asgi:application directly.

  4. channels_redis v4+ host format — v4 prefers connection URLs over tuples. If you're on v4+, switch to:

    python

    "hosts": ["redis://127.0.0.1:6379"]

I wrote a small diagnostic script that checks all of these against your actual settings and prints a PASS/FAIL report: diagnose_channels_redis.py. Run it from your project root (python diagnose_channels_redis.py) and it'll tell you exactly which of the above is the culprit.

Q: Parse Large Json File ( around 300 Mb ) to list of POJO A:

For huge big json file, you should use jackson stream api. You can find the document here. It cost little memory than normal way. In general, your POJO must satisfy certain shapes, it should be able to be separated into many independent parts. Such as a list of object. Then with jackson stream api, you can achieve the object in the list one by one.

Q: Create custom PowerShell Objects from multiple variables A:

Make them arrays first with an array assignment, then loop through the length of the arrays.

$name, $age, $gender = -split $name, -split $age, -split $gender
for($i = 0; $i -lt $name.length; $i++) { [pscustomobject]@{name=$name[$i];
  age=$age[$i]; gender=$gender[$i]} }

Making sure it's not returning a blank 4th object. & { } allows piping from for().

 & { for($i = 0; $i -lt $name.length; $i++) { [pscustomobject]@{name=$name[$i];
   age=$age[$i];gender=$gender[$i]} } } | measure

Count    : 3
Average  :
Sum      :
Maximum  :
Minimum  :
Property :

Q: Maven error "Archetype catalog is empty" while creating Maven project for WebDriver with TestNG A:

Effective January 15, 2020, The Central Repository no longer supports insecure communication over plain HTTP and requires that all requests to the repository are encrypted over HTTPS.

If you're receiving this error, then you need to replace all URL references to Maven Central with their canonical HTTPS counterparts:

Replace http://repo1.maven.org/maven2/ with https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/

Replace http://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/ with https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/

If for any reason your environment cannot support HTTPS, you have the option of using our dedicated insecure endpoint at http://insecure.repo1.maven.org/maven2/

For further context around the move to HTTPS, please see https://blog.sonatype.com/central-repository-moving-to-https.

Q: Multiple config blocks in angular module A:

Having multiple config blocks in application is not a problem. it should work fine. It is totlly fine to chain configs to keep things isolated like. there should be something else that you are missing here. May be the service providers are not resolved at the time App configuration starts.

Or The module which has the service in it is not resolved at the time of App start up. Make sure the module or services which are used in config block are resolved and available in AppModule at start up.

Q: How to extract valid Python code from .ipynb cells A:

The key insight is that you shouldn't try to strip magic lines — you should transform them so the real Python they contain survives. %time import pandas isn't junk; the import pandas is real code you want to keep.

Here's a stdlib-only transformer (no IPython/nbconvert dependency) that handles all your examples:

python

import ast, json, re

_LINE_MAGIC = re.compile(r"^(\s*)%(\w+)(?:\s+(.*))?$")

_SHELL_ASSIGN = re.compile(r'^(\s*)([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*=\s*!(.*)$')

_SHELL_ESCAPE = re.compile(r"^(\s*)!(.*)$")

_CELL_MAGIC = re.compile(r"^(\s*)%%(\w+)")

def _looks_like_real_code(text):

"""True if text is a real Python statement, False if it's a magic

argument like 'inline' (from %matplotlib inline)."""

try**:**

    mod **= ast.parse(text)**

except SyntaxError:

return False

if len(mod.body) != 1:

return True

node **= mod.body\[0\]**

# A bare Name or Constant (e.g. `inline`, `42`) is a magic arg, not code

if isinstance(node, ast.Expr) and isinstance(node.value, (ast.Name, ast.Constant)):

return False

return True

def transform_line(line):

# Shell assignment: var = !cmd -> var = ''

m **= \_SHELL_ASSIGN.match(line)**

if m:

return f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)} = ''"

# Line magic: %magic <code> -> keep <code> if it's real Python

m **= \_LINE_MAGIC.match(line)**

if m:

    indent, magic, rest **= m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3)**

if rest and rest.strip() and _looks_like_real_code(rest.strip()):

return f"{indent}{rest.strip()}"

return f"{indent}pass # %{magic}"

# Bare shell escape: !cmd -> pass

m **= \_SHELL_ESCAPE.match(line)**

if m:

return f"{m.group(1)}pass # was: !{m.group(2).strip()}"

return line

def clean_cell(source):

"""Transform a code cell's source into ast-parseable Python.

Returns None if the cell is a cell-magic (%%bash etc.) and should be skipped."""

lines **= source.splitlines()**

# If first non-blank line is a cell magic, skip the whole cell

for line in lines:

if line.strip() and _CELL_MAGIC.match(line.strip()):

return None

return "\n".join(transform_line(ln) for ln in lines)

Usage:

python

notebook = json.load(open("notebook.ipynb"))

for cell in notebook["cells"]:

if cell.get("cell_type") != "code":

continue

source **= "".join(cell\["source"\]) if isinstance(cell\["source"\], list) else cell\["source"\]**

cleaned **= clean_cell(source)**

if cleaned is None:

continue # cell magic (%%bash) — skip

module **= ast.parse(cleaned)  # now safe — no SyntaxError**

for node in module.body:

    ...  **# work with AST nodes**

This handles all your cases: %time import pandas → import pandas, output = !nvidia-smi → output = '', %%bash cells get skipped, and crucially %matplotlib inline → pass (because inline is a magic argument, not code — caught by the _looks_like_real_code heuristic).

Q: Signing with maven-gpg-plugin hangs intermittently due to missing passphrase A:

Alright, I had a feeling that it was some silly thing.
Turns out that there was a subtle mistake in the settings.xml (which probably would have been obvious if I had pasted the entire file instead of just the <server> snippet). The gpg.passphrase settings never actually made it to the GPG plugin, and the only reason the setup seemed to work, was because I initially pasted the passphrase directly into the plugin configuration (before replacing it with the variable), and gpg-agent will not ask again for the passphrase for 10 minutes by default. The second-to-last paragraph contained all the clues.

To force gpg-agent to ask for the password every time, you can either reset the agent every time (gpgconf --kill gpg-agent) or set the default-cache-ttl configuration option to a suitably low value.

As a side note, this sort of default behavior of GPG does not seem very secure. For a 10-minute time window (after legitimate authorization via passphrase), an unauthorized person or process could make use of the key.
